- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 5–10 days; if below, increase by 1–3%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment >0.5 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to “smooth” extremes; avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment shifts.
